chapter: Porgy and Bess and Varsity Show
title: Back in America in December 1936 with no picture arranged
summary: He refuses other bookings and waits for the promised picture, suspecting Nazarro had paid to get them in a film.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Did you perform on the boat on the way back?

No. No. We come back and we arrive in America in December 1936. I shall never forget. So the next couple of days we contacted the office to find out what the name of the picture was and what studio it was that we were going to be in and so forth, and he said they had no picture -- no, he said at that time, why did I need to know. I said I want to know because I'm not interested in anything else. And he had some bookings for us to go to some theater, I don't know where it was, but I told him I ain't going to take no bookings. Nothing but that picture and I had enough money saved up to lay off and do no other job until I got that picture. And that's what happened. That's what made me think that he must have paid them to put us in a picture because they didn't
Had he written to you what the movie was?
